label: <DEL> step of mid-length sequences starting with s and rich in f/p/g/o/r/j
explanation: Very sparse feature that fires only at the delimiter step (100% of mass), almost always when the first original token (the one about to be output) is s (94% of mass). It favors L=5-7 (98% of mass, peak L=6) and sequences whose remaining tokens are drawn from a small set of letters, mainly f, p, g, o, r, j (also h). More of these letters goes with larger activations: requiring >=4 of them keeps 48% of mass at 30% precision. It never fires in the original or copy phases, and almost never when the first token is not s (rare weak cases with f/n/c/w/q). Precision is low (~9%): many <DEL> steps with first token s and similar letter content stay silent, so the exact conjunction that drives it is not captured. This looks like the tail of a hidden-state direction that encodes s at position 0 together with a particular mix of letters.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 34 cues. Raise it: phase=1 & out_tok=s (+4.23), orig2=p (+2.66), prev_tok=r (+1.62), orig2=f (+1.54), orig3=p (+1.45), next_out=s (+1.20). Lower it: in_first=0 (-2.01), L=9 (-1.66), in_count=1 (-1.53), orig4=- (-1.42).
